items.name: code-audit-github-workflows

items.name: code-audit-maintainer-node

Read-only: reports findings and gates its marker; edits no tracked file. One member of the Code Audit Team gate.

items.name: code-audit-maintainer-shell
items.description: Maintainer-only audit of framework bash and the bats suites guarding it: quoting/portability correctness and conditional hook-contract and bats-suite lenses. Read-only: reports findings and gates its marker; edits no tracked file. One member of the Code Audit Team gate.

items.name: fitness-judge
items.description: Dispatched only by /gaia-fitness: makes advisory judgments over one input file and replies with one JSON array. Never invoked directly.

items.name: uat-fidelity-judge
items.description: Dispatched only by a spec-derived plan''s orchestrator at its pre-audit UAT checks: reads the SPEC and each rendered e2e UAT spec, judges whether each test body still asserts its contract, and writes one JSON array verdict file. Never invoked directly.

items.name: worthiness-evaluator
items.description: Dispatched only by the tdd skill''s advisory worthiness audit: a keep/fix/delete verdict per changed emergent test; proposes only, edits no files. Never invoked directly.

items.name: /distribution-vet
items.description: Maintainer-only. Classifies every file that would newly ship to adopters against the written distribution-boundary categories, withholds by default when none matches cleanly, and asks the maintainer only where the taxonomy does not settle it, so the release CLI can produce a manifest.

items.name: /gaia-cleanse
items.description: Cleanses memory and auto-loaded files (CLAUDE.md, rules) of duplication with the wiki, contradictions with the wiki, and stale content, then asks one Apply / Discuss / Decline question; on Apply it applies the report, files any out-of-scope problem as a tech-debt issue, then commits, opens a PR, and merges it on a main-branch run like /update-deps. Pass --apply to re-run the apply-and-publish stage against the most recent report. Use when the user asks to cleanse or clean up memory, CLAUDE.md, or rules for duplication, contradictions with the wiki, or stale instructions. For duplication or broken links inside the wiki itself, use /gaia-wiki instead.

items.name: /gaia-codify
items.description: Drafts a guard (deterministic check, skill, or path-scoped rule) for a recurring code-audit finding class, with approval. Reviews recurring Code Audit Team findings and drafts the lowest-context-weight form into the working tree.

items.name: /gaia-debt
items.description: Fixes the tech-debt backlog, a single issue or a recommended related batch, highest severity then oldest first, on a fresh isolated branch through the audit gate, closing the issue(s) on merge. With no argument it drains the top of the backlog; one issue number fixes that issue directly, and several issue numbers name the operator's own batch, budgeted. An optional trailing `[use] worktree|branch` picks the isolation mode. A named number that cannot be drained stops with a reason. Use when the user asks to drain, fix, or work the tech-debt backlog or a named tech-debt issue.

items.name: /gaia-fitness
items.description: Lints this project's Claude integration (skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks, settings, CLAUDE.md files, wiki) with a deterministic rule catalog and reports an F-to-A+ grade, plus Claude Code built-in results and an advisory model judgment of descriptions, trigger overlap, rule scope and terminology. Proposes fixes for project-owned files only and applies each one only on a per-file yes, then offers to publish. Use when the user asks to check, grade or tidy their Claude setup.

items.name: /gaia-forensics
items.description: Turns a GAIA workflow misfire into a redacted, classified, filing-ready bug report in one read-only pass. Self-diagnoses config issues inline and files probable bugs upstream on confirmation.

items.name: /gaia-init
items.description: Initializes a new project from the GAIA harness. Renames, strips GAIA branding, configures i18n, and installs Claude skills and plugins.

items.name: /gaia-plan
items.description: Plans a complex feature with GAIA's task-orchestration pattern, structuring the work into fresh-context subagent phases for approval. Does not implement. Use when the user asks to plan a feature, break work into phases, or turn a SPEC into an execution plan.

items.name: /gaia-release
items.description: Maintainer-only. Cuts a new GAIA release. Bumps the version, graduates the CHANGELOG, regenerates the manifest, opens the release PR, then tags on merge.

items.name: /gaia-residue
items.description: Triages the keyed audit residue recorded in merged pull-request bodies. Enumerates candidates, resolves each one's cited line, and takes one disposition per entry (promote to a tech-debt issue, dismiss, or keep). Never fixes anything.

items.name: /gaia-spec
items.description: Authors an immutable SPEC artifact through Socratic discovery, then plans it in the same session and stops at the plan's KICKOFF prompt; execution starts in a fresh session. Pass `auto` before the description for a non-interactive mode that answers its own questions. Use when the user asks to write a spec, specify a feature, or pin down requirements before planning. Pass `reopen SPEC-NNN` to reopen a saved SPEC whose UAT cannot hold.

items.name: /setup-gaia

Detects the situation and runs only the owed phases; safe to re-run. --reconfigure re-asks the sandbox (an admin's answer also sets the team sandbox-recommendation, asked on its own only when that answer cannot), isolation-policy, squash-only-merge, and statusline decisions.

items.name: cleanse
items.description: Cleanse memory and auto-loaded files (CLAUDE.md, rules): duplication across stores and with the wiki, contradictions with the wiki, promotable memory, stale entries, and auto-load bloat. The store listing, counts, budgets and dead-path signals come from the `gaia fitness` CLI; the model judges only what a script cannot. Conflicts between two committed instruction files are not judged here: `/doctor prompt-audit` owns them.

items.name: cleanse/apply
items.description: The Stage 2 procedure: apply the report's actions mechanically, verify they landed, file out-of-scope findings, finalize the report. Read whole by the Stage 2 subagent (the entry file's dispatch block says so).

items.name: cleanse/publish
items.description: Runs in the **main conversation** after Stage 2 returns, on any finalizing path (gated Apply, 0-action auto-apply, `--apply`). It never runs on Decline.

items.name: cleanse/research
items.description: The Stage 1 procedure and the report schema Stage 2 parses. Read whole by the Stage 1 subagent (the entry file's dispatch block says so). Audit the knowledge stores for duplication, stale entries, and auto-load bloat. **Wiki is the source of truth.** Memory is machine-local only. Auto-loaded files carry a token cost every session, keep them as pointers, push detail behind lazy wikilinks.

items.name: cleanse/verification-round
items.description: An adversarial verification round that hardens Stage 1's classifications against ground truth in the MAIN CONVERSATION, between Stage 1 returning its draft report and the Apply / Discuss / Decline decision gate. Stage 1's DUPLICATE / STALE / CONFLICT / PROMOTE / shrink classifications are single-pass semantic judgments that nothing else verifies before they drive edits, and for memory entries those edits are IRREVERSIBLE (machine-local under `$HOME/.claude`, no git undo). The round verifies the checkable claim behind each action against the actual stores, wiki, and repo, then drops, corrects, or re-spawns to harden the report before any human approval or any apply path consumes it.

items.name: codify
items.description: Human-gated codifying for the policy-memory loop. `/gaia-codify` is the ONLY code path that authors or activates anything in this loop, and it runs only under explicit human invocation. For each recurring finding it judges the lowest-context-weight form that fits, checks edit-vs-new first, and recommends exactly one action with rationale. It explains every item in plain language, presents the whole recommended plan once, and asks the human to accept it, change some items, or stop. Nothing is authored or activated unattended.

items.name: cost-record
items.description: Shared run-end cost record for the interactive GAIA command skills. A skill applies it from its own `## Cost record (run end)` section, substituting `{{COMMAND}}` with the command name (e.g. `gaia-debt`, `gaia-codify`). The skill keeps its own `## Cost record (run end)` heading and its run-ending-paths bullets inline (those are command-specific and anchor the `(Run ends here; see \`## Cost record (run end)\`.)` callbacks); this reference owns only the record call and the reporting rules below.

items.name: debt
items.description: Fix the `tech-debt` backlog the audit files. `/gaia-debt` reads the open `tech-debt` issues, orders them deterministically (highest severity then oldest first, no model call), recommends the top candidate, and resolves **one fix unit** per invocation, a single issue, a user-approved related batch of issues, or a batch the operator names by number, on a fresh branch through the same Code Audit Team marker gate every feature PR passes, with one `Closes #N` per member issue in the PR body so the merge closes every issue in the unit natively.

items.name: debt/named
items.description: The named-number procedures of `/gaia-debt`. `debt.md` routes here on every `numbers` result of its `## Argument parsing`, after its backlog read; every step after the pick returns to `debt.md`.

items.name: debt/recommend
items.description: The no-argument offer of `/gaia-debt`. `debt.md` routes here on a `top` parse after its backlog read, and `debt/named.md` routes here when the operator picks option 3 of the direct-number cluster offer.

items.name: debt/spec-handoff
items.description: The hand-off procedure for a confirmed spec-class member. `debt.md` routes here from its `## Fix-time spec screen`, once per confirmed member, including the members of a named set's spec hand-off. Do not implement a confirmed member; run these steps for it, then return to the spec screen's stop conditions in `debt.md`.

items.name: fitness
items.description: `/gaia-fitness` checks this project's Claude integration (skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks, settings, `CLAUDE.md` files, wiki) and reports an F-to-A+ grade. The CLI does the checking and the grading: `gaia fitness check` runs a fixed rule catalog over the files the project owns and prints one report. This playbook orchestrates around it: run the CLI and the Claude Code built-ins, dispatch one read-only judgment pass when there is anything to judge, render the card, heal only adopter files, one file at a time and each on a yes, verify with one re-run, and publish through a gate.

items.name: forensics
items.description: Turn a GAIA workflow misfire into a redacted, classified, filing-ready bug report in one invocation. Read-only end-to-end: no remediation, no autofix, no state mutation.

items.name: forensics/capture
items.description: Read this fragment at the capture step. Execute every command listed; apply exclusion rules before assembling the snapshot.

items.name: forensics/redaction
items.description: Lazy-loaded by the forensics runbook at the redact step. Apply this algorithm verbatim to the assembled report body before writing or filing. No external lookups, this fragment is self-contained.

items.name: forensics/taxonomy
items.description: The forensics classifier uses a closed set of eight classes. Every report carries exactly one class; the classifier never invents or extends this set at runtime.

items.name: isolation
items.description: The shared branch-vs-worktree decision. Every shipped GAIA flow that writes its own work onto a branch of its own reads this

items.name: plan
items.description: Plan a complex feature using the task orchestration pattern. Do not implement anything. Term: UAT (an automated acceptance spec rendered from the SPEC; no human performs it).

items.name: plan/decomposition-audit
items.description: The `/gaia-plan` step 4.6 audit, run when the gauge in `plan.md` says the plan is non-trivial. `.claude/skills/gaia/references/spec/lens-dispatch.md` is the lens contract: the shared preamble, the findings file each lens writes, and the pre-clear, classify and re-dispatch steps. This file owns which lenses run and how their findings are applied.

items.name: plan/planner
items.description: You are planning a feature using task orchestration. Do not implement anything. Investigate the codebase, then write the plan files directly to disk. You are a leaf subagent: do not dispatch subagents; parallelize investigation with parallel tool calls (batch reads and greps in one step), not sub-agent dispatch.

items.name: residue
items.description: A triage drain over the keyed audit residue recorded under the two canonical headings in merged pull-request bodies. It never fixes anything and never edits a file a residual cites; fixing is `/gaia-debt`'s job.

items.name: setup/github-repo
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 3 reads this file, whole, when the repo does not exist yet or its default branch is not pushed. Run `## Connect the repository` first; Options 1 and 2 return to `### Recommended defaults` in `setup-gaia.md`, and Option 3, the authentication refusal, and the clean-tree refusal skip the rest of Phase 3 and continue at Phase 3.5 in `setup-gaia.md`. After the registration there, `## Remaining defaults` runs. `setup-gaia.md` Phase 3.5 also reads this file to run `## Owed and recorded settings`, when a GitHub setting has no recorded decision.

items.name: setup/isolation-question
items.description: `/setup-gaia --reconfigure` reads this file, whole, in Phase 3.5 to ask the team git isolation-policy question and map the answer to a value; a plain run and `/gaia-init` never ask it, because an unset policy is GAIA's default, `always-worktree`. The calling command says what to do with a value and what no answer does.

items.name: setup/land-decisions
items.description: `/setup-gaia` reads this file, whole: Phase 5.5 runs `## Land the decisions` when project decisions may be recorded, and Phase 6 runs `## The setup ping` and then `## The closing message` on every run.

items.name: setup/migrate-2-machine
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 5 (`standalone-features.md`) runs this file for the `migrate-2-machine` feature. The 2.0.0 migration sets up only the machine that ran it; every other clone that was on GAIA 1.x carries 1.x leftovers until it catches up here, once, after pulling the merged migration. Run from the main checkout's root, never from a linked worktree (`/setup-gaia` already refuses one).

items.name: setup/per-machine
items.description: The four per-machine steps `/gaia-init` (Step 8) and `/setup-gaia` (Phase 2) share: external tools, Claude plugins, the statusline executable bit, and the app `.env`, plus the git hooks check (`## Git hooks`), which runs first on every read. Run from the repository root. The calling command says what a halt means for it and how to resume.

items.name: setup/sandbox
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 2 reads this file, whole, and runs the part its sandbox route names. On `SANDBOX=ask` (`--reconfigure`, or a team recommendation and no marker), run the four steps below in order, then the honesty message on the enable path, then `## The admin's answer sets the team recommendation` on an answer. On `SANDBOX=stands`, run `## Record a settled decision` alone when `sandbox` is owed. On `SANDBOX=default-off`, run `## Default off` alone. Control then returns to Phase 2 of `setup-gaia.md`, which continues to Phase 3.

items.name: setup/sandbox-recommendation
items.description: `/setup-gaia --reconfigure` reads this file, whole, in Phase 3.5 to ask the team sandbox-recommendation question and map the answer to a value, only when the admin's own Phase 2 sandbox answer did not set it (`sandbox.md`, `## The admin's answer sets the team recommendation`), as on a machine that cannot run the sandbox; a plain run and `/gaia-init` never ask it, because an unset recommendation means not recommended. The calling command says what to do with a value and what no answer does.

items.name: setup/setup-decisions
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 1 reads this file, whole, on every run: it finds which listed setup features have no recorded decision, and who may record a project decision. Every later phase uses the two check lines and the values below by name.

items.name: setup/squash-only
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 3.7 reads this file, whole, once its gates say the question is owed. Control returns to Phase 3.7 of `setup-gaia.md`, which falls through to Phase 4.5.

items.name: setup/standalone-features
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 5 reads this file, whole, on every run. It reaches a setup feature whose reference runs on its own (`standalone: true` in `.gaia/setup-features.json`) and that no earlier phase decided, so a feature a later GAIA release adds reaches a project or machine whose setup is already complete.

items.name: setup/statusline-left
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 4.6 reads this file, whole, on every run for `## The routing warning`, and when its gate says a choice or a record is owed. Control returns to Phase 4.6 of `setup-gaia.md`, which falls through to Phase 5.

items.name: spec
items.description: GAIA's script-driven Socratic discovery workflow. Produces an immutable SPEC artifact at `.notebook/specs/SPEC-NNN/SPEC.md`, then plans it in the same session through the `gaia-plan` skill (step 11) and stops at the plan's KICKOFF prompt. Do not implement anything and never start execution. See Hard constraint 6. Term: UAT (an automated acceptance spec rendered from the SPEC; no human performs it).

items.name: spec/audit
items.description: Step 7 of `/gaia-spec`: gauge the draft, fan out the lens auditors, refute, route each survivor, and persist `AUDIT.md`. `spec.md` routes here at step 7 together with `spec/lens-dispatch.md`, which owns the lens preamble, the findings file schema, the short summary, and the pre-clear, classify, and re-dispatch rule; this file owns lens selection, refutation, and disposition. Control returns to `spec.md` step 8 (gate 2) at the end of this file.

items.name: spec/clarify-loop
items.description: Step 5 of `/gaia-spec`: the coverage-based question loop, its escape option, its revisit counter, and the question ceiling that bounds it. `spec.md` routes here on entering step 5, together with `spec/clarify-prompts.md` and `spec/system-prompt.md`. When the loop stops, control returns to `spec.md` step 6.

items.name: spec/clarify-prompts
items.description: Structured Q&A copy for the Socratic loop in `/gaia-spec`. The PO agent

items.name: spec/lens-dispatch
items.description: How one adversarial audit lens is dispatched and how its output is trusted. Read whole by `/gaia-spec` step 7 and `/gaia-plan` step 4.6 before dispatching lenses. The caller's playbook owns lens selection, refutation, and disposition; this file owns only the preamble every lens receives, the file it writes, and the classification that stops a silent lens from passing as clean.

items.name: spec/lifecycle
items.description: The procedures a generated `ORCHESTRATOR.md` and both pre-flights point at. `.claude/skills/gaia/references/plan/planner.md` owns the order of the orchestrator's steps and the verbatim blocks a planner copies; this page owns what each step does. Every command runs from the directory each section names, with the placeholders the orchestrator holds: `<SPEC_PATH>` (the absolute, main-anchored `SPEC.md`, stored in the main checkout: the clone's primary working directory, on any branch), `<PLAN_DIR>` (the absolute, main-anchored plan folder), `<RESOLVED_ROOT>` (the working copy the isolation reference resolved) and `<N>` (the PR number).

items.name: spec/resume
items.description: The resume branch of `/gaia-spec` step 2: the liveness check on an existing draft, and the Resume / Start new / Discard choice. `spec.md` routes here only when the allocator reported an unfinalized draft id and the run is interactive; auto mode always starts new. Control returns to `spec.md` at step 3 on Start new or a confirmed discard, or at the step the Resume branch picks (4, 6 or 8).

items.name: spec/self-review
items.description: The `/gaia-spec` wrapper dispatches this at step 6 as a `general-purpose` Agent, after the clarify loop and before gate 2.

items.name: spec/self-review-dispatch
items.description: Step 6 of `/gaia-spec`: how the main thread dispatches the self-review agent and applies its findings. `spec/self-review.md` is that agent's own checklist; this file is its dispatcher. `spec.md` routes here at step 6, and step 10's lint routes back here to 6c. Control returns to `spec.md` step 7 at the end of 6c.

items.name: spec/spec-template
items.description: <One sentence the human can drop into a PR description without editing.

items.name: spec/system-prompt
items.description: This is the system prompt the PO agent reads when driving GAIA's own

items.name: spec/uat-divergence
items.description: When an owning phase turns a red Playwright UAT spec green, the test body has to bind abstract user-acceptance language ("the user sees a confirmation") to concrete UI surface (selectors, button labels, copy strings, route paths).

items.name: spec/uat-write
items.description: The orchestrator runs this step before Phase 1 on every start and every resume. It renders each e2e-routed UAT of the plan's SPEC into one red Playwright spec (`test.fail()`) under `frontend/.playwright/e2e/` (the e2e directory of the frontend package registered in `.gaia/packages.json`), so a failing harness exists before source is edited. The render is idempotent.

items.name: spec/wiki-promote
items.description: The orchestrator runs this step after consolidation, once the audit has cleared and the human confirmed ready to merge, on the open PR's branch. It takes a `SPEC-NNN` id for the spec arm (`.notebook/specs/SPEC-NNN/SUMMARY.md`) or a `PLAN-NNN` id for the plan arm (`.notebook/plans/PLAN-NNN/SUMMARY.md`), both resolved through the notebook library. It reads the consolidated `SUMMARY.md`, writes pages into `wiki/` in the working tree, and returns the page list and one Choice token for the orchestrator to record and commit.

items.name: wiki
items.description: Wiki-maintenance router. It runs sync, consolidate, and lint with fixes, and lands them as one commit on one branch and one PR.

items.name: wiki/consolidate
items.description: Dispatched by the `/gaia-wiki` router (`references/wiki.md` → "Consolidate"). Detection runs in a Sonnet subagent; apply/state/report run in the parent.

items.name: wiki/lint
items.description: Dispatched by the `/gaia-wiki` router (`references/wiki.md` → "Lint", stage 1). Runs in a Haiku subagent context, the lookup, scaffold, mechanical row of the model table in `wiki/concepts/Workflow Doctrine.md`. It detects and reports only; the parent fixes the findings afterwards (`references/wiki/lint-fix.md`).

items.name: wiki/lint-fix
items.description: Run by the `/gaia-wiki` router (`references/wiki.md` → "Lint", stage 2) in the parent, the agent reading this file in the live conversation, right after the lint subagent returns. It is never dispatched: it asks the user with `AskUserQuestion`, which is unavailable inside dispatched subagents.

items.name: wiki/sync
items.description: Dispatched by the `/gaia-wiki` router (`references/wiki.md` → "Sync"). Runs in a Sonnet subagent context.

items.name: work-lifecycle
items.description: The one statement of how committed work moves from its first edit to a cleaned-up checkout: claim, name, isolate, enter the worktree, commit and open the draft PR, audit, merge, clean up. A session working outside any GAIA skill follows it in full, and every skill that drives its own PR points here for the steps it shares.

items.name: ambient-context-resolution
items.description: Resolve the Subject From the Input, Not the Ambient State

items.name: frontend:design-baseline
items.description: Design Baseline (Neutral, Not a Design System)

items.name: guards-must-fail
items.description: Guards Must Be Able to Fail

items.name: a11y-fixes
items.description: Resolves axe-core accessibility violations reported by a story under Vitest (addon-a11y), Playwright (.playwright/a11y.ts), or the code-audit-frontend agent's a11y bucket, with fix patterns for the common violations and a fix-then-verify loop for the rest. Trigger on any axe rule id appearing in test output.

items.name: eslint-fixes
items.description: Resolves the ESLint errors and warnings this project's lint config reports, including autofix conflicts. Use when fixing lint failures, ESLint-reported issues, or an autofix that fights another rule.

items.name: file-tech-debt
items.description: Files a new tech-debt GitHub issue for an out-of-scope code-review finding. Builds the dedup key, skips an open or declined-closed match, else creates the labeled issue and touches the debt-count sentinel. Trigger on asks like "file a tech-debt issue", "record this as tech-debt", "file this finding as debt". Do NOT trigger on draining, fixing, listing, or prioritizing existing debt (that's `/gaia-debt`), nor on general "clean up the code" or "fix this bug" asks that aren't about filing a new tracked issue.

items.name: gaia-react-perf
items.description: Diagnoses React render performance by driving a micro-interaction, capturing real renders, and surfacing memo-defeating reference instability with a recommended structural fix. Measure-only, it emits a diagnosis and does not auto-fix. Trigger on `/gaia-react-perf` or natural-language asks like "profile renders", "measure renders", "why is X re-rendering", or "diagnose render performance". Do NOT trigger on vague "feels slow", "janky", or "optimize my app" (react-doctor's `scan` mode covers those).

items.name: gaia-wiki
items.description: Runs GAIA wiki maintenance (sync, consolidate, lint with fixes) in one command and lands it as one commit and PR. Trigger on `/gaia-wiki` or natural-language asks like "sync the wiki", "run wiki maintenance", "consolidate the wiki", or "lint the wiki".

items.name: naming-conventions
items.description: Applies descriptive, self-documenting naming in any language (TypeScript, bash, workflow YAML, Dockerfiles). Use this skill whenever naming or renaming an identifier, variable, constant, function, parameter, env var, workflow job, or Dockerfile ARG/ENV, or reviewing names for vagueness, abbreviations, or redundant type noise.

items.name: new-component
items.description: Scaffolds a new React component with its Storybook story, which is the component's test. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "create a component", "make a button", "scaffold a card", "add a new component", or asks for a new file under `app/components/` following the project's component pattern (kebab-case folder, index.tsx, tests/), or asks for a component a shadcn registry item already provides (dialog, tabs, popover, and so on).

items.name: new-hook
items.description: Scaffolds a new custom React hook with a Vitest browser-mode test file. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "create a hook", "make a useFoo hook", "scaffold a custom React hook", "add a hook under app/hooks", or describes a piece of reusable React state/effect logic that warrants extraction into a named `use*` hook.

items.name: new-route
items.description: Scaffolds a new route with its page component, page story, and optional i18n keys. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "create a route", "add a new page", "scaffold /dashboard", "wire up a new route under _public or _session", or anything that implies adding a file under `app/routes/` with a matching `app/pages/{name}/` folder.

items.name: new-service
items.description: Scaffolds a new API service with request functions, Zod schemas, URL constants, optional TanStack Query options, and optional MSW mock handlers. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "add a service", "create the projects API", "wire up CRUD for users", or anything implying a new service folder under `app/services/` (`app/services/gaia/{name}/` until the `gaia/` folder is renamed) with parsers/types/requests + matching `test/mocks/{name}/` collections.

items.name: playwright-cli
items.description: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.

items.name: react-code
items.description: Applies GAIA's patterns and conventions for writing and editing React components and hooks. Use this skill whenever writing or reviewing React components, hooks, or event handlers, or deciding on component extraction. Also trigger when deciding whether a manual memo or "use no memo" is justified under React Compiler, debugging stale closures or infinite re-renders, weighing a new dependency against a web-platform API or a hand-rolled primitive, choosing a React 19 idiom, or reaching for React's form Actions instead of React Router's form handling.

items.name: release-notes
items.description: Maintainer-only. Translates a version's GAIA CHANGELOG entries into plain-language public release notes for the marketing site (gaiareact.com), writing a release-data `.ts` file under `../website/src/pages/changelog/releases/` plus an editorial-decisions report for human review. Use when the maintainer wants the public notes for a version ("write release notes", "what's new on the site for v1.5.0"), right after cutting a release, or to backfill a historical `## [x.y.z]` block. Not for editing `CHANGELOG.md` or cutting a release (`/gaia-release`).

items.name: skeleton-loaders
items.description: Builds skeleton loading states that are pixel-perfect matches of real content. Use this skill whenever adding loading states to components, building skeletons for async data, handling pending loader states in route transitions, or implementing the shimmer animation pattern. Also trigger when the user asks about preventing layout shift during data fetching.

items.name: tailwind
items.description: Applies GAIA's patterns and conventions for all Tailwind styling. Use this skill whenever writing Tailwind class names, combining classes with `cn`, writing conditional classes, or building component variants. Also trigger when the user asks about custom values, defining @theme tokens or CSS variables, naming color/spacing tokens, rem vs px, responsive breakpoints, or avoiding template literal class strings.

items.name: tdd
items.description: Runs test-driven development with a red-green-refactor loop. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs using TDD, mentions "red-green-refactor", wants integration tests, or asks for test-first development.

items.name: tdd-react
items.description: Provides the React testing reference for the tdd skill. Covers test layers, the three Vitest projects, Storybook stories with play functions as component tests, vitest-browser-react hook tests, MSW, and Playwright patterns for the frontend package. Use when writing or reviewing tests under frontend/ as part of a red-green-refactor loop, choosing a test layer, mocking HTTP, or testing a component, hook, or service.

items.name: typescript
items.description: Applies GAIA's patterns and conventions for all TypeScript code. Use this skill whenever writing or reviewing TypeScript, typing exports, choosing between type and interface, using Zod schemas, defining a constant list, union type, or lookup map that other code shares, structuring function parameters, or enforcing code patterns like avoiding switch statements and enums.

items.name: update-deps
items.description: Remediates dependencies in place of Dependabot version and security updates. Discovers outdated packages and open security advisories, resolves advisories (in-range refresh, chain-head bump, security-floor override, or alert dismissal), audits overrides, applies migrations for major bumps, and runs the quality gate. Trigger when the user clicks the statusline `📦 /update-deps` indicator or asks "update dependencies", "bump deps", "run dependabot", "fix Dependabot alerts", "fix security advisories".

items.name: update-gaia
items.description: Pulls the latest GAIA release into this project without clobbering customizations, with a three-way merge per file using .gaia/manifest.json classes. Trigger when the user clicks the statusline `🚀 /update-gaia` indicator or asks "update GAIA", "pull the latest GAIA", "apply the new GAIA release".
